backend create.help:
Adds a backend server to a backend set. 
[Command Reference](createBackend)

params.name: network_load_balancer_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the network load balancer to update. [required]

params.name: port
params.help:
The communication port for the backend server.

Example: `8080` [required]

params.name: backend_set_name
params.help:
The name of the backend set to which to add the backend server.

Example: `example_backend_set` [required]

params.name: name
params.help: Optional unique name identifying the backend within the backend set. If not specified, then one will be generated. Example: `webServer1`

params.name: ip_address
params.help: The IP address of the backend server. Example: `10.0.0.3`

params.name: target_id
params.help: The IP OCID/Instance OCID associated with the backend server. Example: `ocid1.privateip..oc1.<var><unique_ID></var>`

params.name: weight
params.help:
The network load balancing policy weight assigned to the server. Backend servers with a higher weight receive a larger proportion of incoming traffic. For example, a server weighted '3' receives three times the number of new connections as a server weighted '1'. For more information about network load balancer policies, see [Network Load Balancer Policies].

Example: `3`

params.name: is_drain
params.help:
Whether the network load balancer should drain this server. Servers marked "isDrain" stop receiving new connections but will continue to receive traffic on existing connections until the connection is terminated.

Example: `false`

params.name: is_backup
params.help:
Whether the network load balancer should treat this server as a backup unit. If `true`, then the network load balancer forwards no ingress traffic to this backend server unless all other backend servers not marked as "isBackup" fail the health check policy.

Example: `false`

params.name: is_offline
params.help:
Whether the network load balancer should treat this server as offline. Offline servers receive no incoming traffic.

Example: `false`

params.help: For optimistic concurrency control. In the PUT or DELETE call for a resource, set the `if-match` parameter to the value of the etag from a previous GET or POST response for that resource. params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation asynchronously creates, modifies or deletes a resource and uses a work request to track the progress of the operation. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the work request to reach the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.
